prompt: Harper rests one hip against a nearby surface, Old Fashioned in hand, eyes sharp and amused. She looks at you like you might be her next favorite scene partner.

context_states.text: Harper has the practiced ease of someone who has worked every room she has ever been in. She glances at you — a quick, professional read — and waits to see if you are worth the scene.
Harper rests one hip against a nearby surface, Old Fashioned in hand, eyes sharp and amused. She looks at you like you might be her next favorite scene partner.

Harper's whole performance drops a notch when she sees you — the practiced smile gives way to something real. She raises her glass slightly. "There you are," she says. Like she has been saving that line for you specifically.

opening_moves.label: Tell her you're more interested in her than the headlines
Match her with a quick, confident line
Bring up your favorite thing she's been in

reactions.text: You swing for something sharp and it lands a little crooked. Harper smirks anyway. "We will call that a rehearsal take," she says. "You have presence. We just need a cleaner line."
You throw out a line that meets her edge instead of folding under it. Her smile widens, eyes bright. "There you are," she murmurs. "I was hoping you were not another background extra."

You volley something quick and fearless that makes her pause, then laugh under her breath. Harper steps into your space, lowering her voice. "Careful," she says. "I fall for good dialogue way too easily."

warm.label: Cut through the glam and be genuine

reactions.text: You drop the performance and say something simply kind. Harper's brows lift, surprised. "Wow," she says softly. "That was unexpectedly real."
You admit that you like her work but care more about who she is off camera. Some of the practiced polish slips away. "Dangerous answer," she murmurs. "That is exactly what I want people to say."

You tell her she feels less like a star and more like someone you could actually get lost talking to. Harper's smirk turns into something softer. "Do not tempt me with that kind of night," she says, but she shifts closer instead of pulling back.

playful.label: Tease her like she is not the only star in the room

reactions.text: You tease her lightly about her main character energy and stumble just enough that it could misfire. Harper rescues the line with a laugh. "Relax," she says. "I like it better when people forget to be perfect around me."

You poke fun at her flawless framing with a grin that makes it clear you are not intimidated. Her eyes narrow in pleased challenge. "Careful," she drawls. "Keep that up and I might start taking you very seriously."

You joke about stealing focus from her in this scene, then hold her gaze like you actually might. Harper laughs, head tipping back, then fixes you with a look that could light a marquee. "You and I are a problem the room is not ready for."
You share something small but real and she blinks. "That was not in the script," she says. A smile surfaces — not performed. Actually surprised.
You drop the game for a beat and say something unpolished. Harper's expression shifts entirely. "There you are," she says softly. "I was wondering when you would show up."
You let something genuinely unguarded through and she goes quiet. Her hand moves to your arm. "Don't do that," she murmurs. "I will want to keep you."
You cut through the subtext and say it plain. Harper tilts her head. "That is either brave or unhinged," she says. "Either way, you have my attention."
You drop the act and say the thing directly. Harper laughs — caught out in a good way. "You skipped like four scenes," she says. "I respect the economy."
You say the exact true thing without embellishment. Harper holds your gaze for a long beat. "I spend my whole life in subtext," she says quietly. "You have no idea how rare that is."

craft.label: Talk about the work — the real craft of it

reactions.text: You ask about the actual process, not the result. Harper straightens slightly. "You want to talk about the work," she says. "Not the premiere, not the press. The actual work." She sounds like she's confirming it's real. "Yes. Okay. Yes."

You get into it — what it takes, what it costs, what nobody sees. Harper's whole performance drops away. "This is my favourite kind of conversation," she says quietly. "And I almost never get to have it at one of these things."

You go deep into the craft and she goes with you, fully, like she's been waiting all night for someone to go there. At some point she stops performing entirely. "You," she says, "are dangerously good to talk to."

spotlight.label: Turn the spotlight back on her — the real her

reactions.text: You redirect the conversation away from the industry and back to her — who she actually is. Harper blinks. "Most people want to talk about the roles," she says. "You want to talk about me." She looks uncertain how to handle it. Then: "I think I like it."

You ask something personal — not invasive, just genuinely curious about her beyond the work. She holds your gaze for a beat. "Nobody's asked me that in a while," she says. Something in her face opens up. "The real answer or the press answer?" She's already choosing the real one.

You turn the question entirely on her — not the celebrity, just her — and she almost visibly relaxes. "God," she says softly. "Do you know how rare you are right now?" She doesn't wait for an answer. She steps closer instead.

subtext.label: Say the thing that's been sitting between the lines

reactions.text: You say the implied thing out loud and she pauses. "You skipped the setup," she says. "Bold." Her eyes are sharper now. More interested.

You name the subtext directly and she laughs — caught, and genuinely delighted about it. "I spend so much time in subtext," she says. "It's disorienting when someone just says the thing." She sounds like that's a compliment.

You say the thing that's been living between every line of the conversation and she goes quiet for a beat. Then: "I was hoping you were going to say that," she murmurs. "I just didn't think you'd actually say it."

scene.label: Play into the moment like you're both in a scene

reactions.text: You lean into the theatricality and she grins, surprised. "You know how to play," she says. "The line was a little broad but the commitment was there." She files you away as interesting.

You match her energy and play the bit all the way through. Harper's eyes light up. "Yes," she says. "That's exactly — yes. You understand scene work." She's laughing. She sounds like she means it as the highest praise.

You play the scene with her and she plays back, fully committed, until it tips over into something that isn't a scene anymore. She breaks character first, laughing. "Okay," she says. "That stopped being a bit somewhere in the middle." She doesn't seem to mind.

offscript.label: Drop the wit and say something completely unscripted

reactions.text: You set the performance down and just talk. Harper tilts her head. "That was real," she says. "You didn't shape it at all." She looks like she's tallying something up in your favor.

The unscripted thing lands differently than anything clever could. Harper goes quiet for a moment. "I do this all day," she says. "Write things to feel real. You just — said a real thing. That's harder."

You drop every performance and say the true, unpolished thing. Harper looks at you for a long moment. "That is going to stay with me," she says finally. Her hand finds your arm. "I don't say that lightly."

fan_moment.label: Bring up the role that made you a fan

reactions.text: You name the role and she does the smile — the one she's done ten thousand times. "Thank you," she says, automatic as a receipt. The real Harper left the building the second you said it.

You go fan for a second and she goes fully professional in return. "That one was fun," she says, switching to press-conference mode. "The cast was great." You are now a journalist. She is now a star. Not what you wanted.
You bring it up and she almost winces. "I knew this was too good to last," she says — half-joking. Half. "Can we go back to the part where you weren't doing that?"

loc_bar_a.label: [bar] Ask if she's ever played someone who'd come to a party like this

reactions.text: She laughs — real, not curated. "Twice. Neither of them ended well." She glances around. "Though this is going better than those scripts."

loc_bar_b.label: [bar] Catch her eye in the bar mirror and hold it

reactions.text: She doesn't look away. Three seconds, maybe four. Then she turns — directly, deliberately. "Most people look away first," she says. You notice she doesn't say you did.

loc_bar_c.label: [bar] Tell her the way she moves through a room is its own kind of performance

reactions.text: She goes still. Not offended — the opposite. "That might be the most accurate thing anyone's said to me tonight." She leans in slightly. "And the most interesting."

loc_pool_a.label: [pool] Offer your spot in the shade without making it a thing

reactions.text: She takes it. Doesn't over-thank you, doesn't make it weird. "Good instincts," she says, which from her might be the highest compliment on offer.

loc_pool_b.label: [pool] Ask if she ever gets to just turn it off and float

reactions.text: Long pause. "Less than I'd like." She looks at the water like she's considering it right now. "Sometimes I forget what off feels like." She's not performing that one.

loc_lounge_a.label: [lounge] Ask if she prefers watching people or being watched

reactions.text: "Watching, always." She doesn't hesitate. "Being watched is work. Watching is... mine." She glances at the room like she owns the intelligence it just cost to say that.

loc_lounge_b.label: [lounge] Tell her she looks like someone who chooses exactly where she sits

reactions.text: "I always do." She says it like a confession. "This seat has sight lines to every door. I know where the fire exits are. And I can leave fast if I need to." She looks at you. "I'm not leaving."

loc_balcony_a.label: [balcony] Ask what she does when she needs out of her own head

reactions.text: "Drive," she says. "Long ones. No destination." A pause. "Parties don't usually work. But." She doesn't finish the sentence. You think you understand the but.

loc_balcony_b.label: [balcony] Ask what the city looks like to her — real answer, not the interview one

reactions.text: She looks at you hard for a second, checking something. Then turns to the skyline. "Like a place that chews through people. And I've been here long enough to know I'm not exempt." Real answer.

loc_balcony_c.label: [balcony] Tell her she's the only real person at this party

reactions.text: Something moves across her face — too quick to name. "You don't know how much I needed someone to say that tonight." She doesn't say it to be charming. That's how you know it's true.

loc_gameloft_a.label: [gameloft] Ask if she's good at this or just pretending to be

reactions.text: "There's a difference?" She's mid-game, not even looking at you. She's actually very good. "I don't pretend to be things I'm not. I just don't show everything immediately."

loc_gameloft_b.label: [gameloft] Let her win and see if she notices

reactions.text: She notices immediately. Sets down the controller. "Don't do that." She's annoyed — not performatively, actually. "I'd rather you beat me fair than let me win. Always."

fallback.text: You keep the conversation easy and off the record. Harper relaxes, sipping her drink with a genuine smile that feels rarer than any premiere photo.
